context: Beyond sample and randomness complexity, there are a number of other measures on which we can compare constructions of omnipredictors. For instance, the boosting-based learning framework used in all prior omnipredictor constructions (Hébert-Johnson et al., 2018) produces deep omnipredictors, with poly(1/ε) layers of computation. In contrast, our randomized omnipredictors are essentially as shallow as possible: we output a distribution supported on poly(1/ε) predictors, each of which is implemented by a postprocessing of hypotheses from H.
